[1/2] Phase 2 plan

impact_assessment.why: The user's standing goal is that Cairn measures faster than C, C++ and Rust; the scoreboard only measures C (gcc/clang/cl) and Rust (rustc) today, so the claim cannot be tested for C++ at all. contract: additive Case field and new report keys only, existing fields and exit codes unchanged. dependency: C++ compilers already installed (g++ or clang++ or cl) detected the same way as the C row; no new toolchain requirement when absent - C++ verdicts read unavailable. concurrency: single-threaded harness, unchanged. state: history records gain a cpp key; compare_runs reads only the Cairn column, so old records stay comparable.
impact_assessment.benefits: The goal line gains a third verdict per case; 12 .cpp twins widen the parity gate; any C++-vs-C performance split that gcc's C++ frontend produces becomes visible and optimizable.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the TwinParityTest shape changes from triples to quadruples - old tests must keep passing until updated in the same commit. dependency: a broken or exotic C++ installation must degrade to unavailable, never crash the harness. concurrency: none. state: malformed cpp key in history must be skipped like the other baseline keys.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Additive-only schema change with the C build plumbing mirrored; parity gate run before any scoreboard number is recorded; absence of a C++ compiler returns unavailable verdicts and exit 2 only when no baseline at all exists

impact_assessment.why: user goal: for Cairn to be a proper language it needs more functions and constructs than i64 plus print; the gap list stands at for loop, print_char/print_hex, arrays, strings, more than four parameters, structs
impact_assessment.benefits: each milestone is independently committed and gated; for-loops ride the existing While codegen including countdown folding; print_char/print_hex extend the syscall runtime already in place; stack parameters lift the MAX_PARAMETERS limit without breaking the four-register convention
impact_assessment.risks: contract: verify.py gates ten V-rules and capabilities.py publishes language limits, both must move with any syntax change; dependency: none new, still only the Python interpreter; concurrency: none, compilation is single-threaded; state: benchmark history and ledger unchanged, but the PRINCIPLE-004 plan pointer must name this task
impact_assessment.mitigation: new constructs get failing-first parser/sema/codegen tests plus end-to-end value tests; the full suite and --save --compare benchmark gate re-run after every milestone (G-004); SPEC.md and README updated in the same commit as each language change
